title: What Living Art Ecosystems Is
definition: Living Art Ecosystems: artworks that are alive and growing.
description:
Living Art Ecosystems — Signature Edition: artworks that are alive and growing. This is the JAH-original vision, designed from first principles and labeled as Signature speculation throughout.

The Signature ecosystem hulls program starts where public roadmaps stop. Where public research asks what is fundable, the Signature line asks what is buildable: living media rethought, ecosystem logistics rebuilt, care protocols reimagined for the century ahead. Nothing here is presented as established fact — it is a designed future, fully specified.

This edition mirrors the public database record for record — concept, components, milestones, demos, drills, alliance, roadmap — but every entry is the Signature take: bolder timelines, integrated systems thinking, and the evolution ambition that defines the Signature line.

t: The Signature Vision: Living Art Ecosystems
title: The Signature Vision: Living Art Ecosystems
definition: The JAH-original Signature vision of Living Art Ecosystems.
description:
The Signature vision of Living Art Ecosystems does not ask what committees will fund — it asks what physics allows and what engineering can compound.

Signature ecosystem hulls program, charter one: master living media at laboratory scale within the decade. Charter two: scale ecosystem logistics manufacturing until cost collapses. Charter three: operate care protocols systems continuously, learning in public, improving every cycle.

This is a Signature concept — original JAH speculation, fully specified and honestly labeled. The public edition of this database carries the documented research record; this edition carries the bolder integrated vision: what Living Art Ecosystems becomes when every piece is designed to work with every other piece from day one.

title: Readiness Estimator: Living Art Ecosystems
definition: Estimates Living Art Ecosystems readiness from component maturity.
description:
The estimator scores the six Living Art Ecosystems components on the TRL 1–9 scale and averages them into a verdict: research phase, pilot phase, or deployment phase. Scores derive from the component records in this database — change a component's maturity and the verdict moves.

Honest scoring is the point: a ecosystem hulls that averages TRL 3 is not failing, it is three phases from deployment, and the estimator tells you which component drags the average down. Fund that one first.

title: Living Art Ecosystems Systems Simulator
definition: Simulates Living Art Ecosystems operating for a day.
description:
The simulator walks a Living Art Ecosystems installation through six operating steps, with seeded randomness standing in for real-world variation. Seed 51873 reproduces this exact run — change the seed in the program to explore other days.

Watch for DEGRADED steps: they mark where living media monitoring, ecosystem logistics redundancy, or care protocols maintenance would intervene in a real deployment. A simulator that never degrades is lying; this one degrades about eight percent of the time, like early hardware does.

title: Living Art Ecosystems Master Roadmap
definition: The united roadmap for Living Art Ecosystems: prove, build, operate, compound.
description:
The master roadmap for Living Art Ecosystems — artworks that are alive and growing.

Phase 1 — Prove (living media): laboratory demonstrations of every component, replicated independently. No scaling until the physics is boring.

Phase 2 — Build (ecosystem logistics): pilot manufacturing and integration. The six pieces meet for the first time and the interfaces get honest.

Phase 3 — Operate (care protocols): continuous real-world operation. Uptime, cost curves and failure data replace projections.

Phase 4 — Compound (evolution): ecosystem hulls as everyday infrastructure. Costs collapse, standards settle, and galleries-scale deployment begins.

Signature edition: phases overlap aggressively — integration starts on day one. This record unites the database: overview, research, components, milestones, demos and drills all point here.
key_points: Four phases: Prove, Build, Operate, Compound.
Each phase has exit criteria.
Unites all 20 records.
